claims.statement: Texas Bulletin B-2021-08 applies to residential property policies delivered or issued for delivery in Texas with an effective date on or after 2022-01-01, while HO 01 45 2022-01 applies to policies effective on or after that date, attaches to HO-3, and controls if it conflicts with the attached form.

The Texas Homeowners Appetite Guide is internal underwriting guidance rather than policy contract language, and its wind/hail section directs underwriters to the applicable state amendment and Department requirements rather than prior-year rating output.

HO-3 2018-09 S.5 uses the Declarations deductible for each Section I loss, recognizes a separate windstorm/hail deductible where a state amendment requires it, and otherwise selects only the larger when both apply; HO 01 45 T.1 expressly amends S.5 for a Texas wind/hail loss.

Under Bulletin B-2021-08 B.2, a separate windstorm/hail deductible may be 1% through 5% of Coverage A, with a 10% maximum in B.6 seacoast territories, or a flat dollar amount no lower than the all-other-perils deductible; B.7 requires filing of the amendatory endorsement and rate rule before the deductible may be applied.

HO 01 45 T.1 contractually specifies a separate windstorm/hail deductible stated in the Declarations as a percentage of Coverage A, generally 1% through 5% and up to 10% in its seacoast territories; the bulletin's flat-dollar permission is not HO 01 45 contract wording.

Bulletin B-2021-08 B.4 requires the separate windstorm/hail deductible on the Declarations page in type no smaller than the all-other-perils deductible and requires both the percentage and the resulting dollar amount at the Coverage A limit in effect at issuance.

A windstorm/hail deductible percentage increase requires written notice at least 30 days before the renewal effective date; without notice, the increase is ineffective for that renewal term and the prior percentage continues under both B.4 and HO 01 45 T.2.

For a windstorm or hail loss under HO 01 45 T.1, only the separate windstorm/hail deductible applies and the all-other-perils deductible is not also applied; Bulletin B-2021-08 B.3 states the same regulatory nonstacking requirement.

For one occurrence involving wind/hail and another covered peril, B.3 and HO 01 45 T.1 apply each deductible to its separately determinable damage portion, but require only the larger single deductible for the entire loss when the portions cannot be separately determined.

When the Declarations select a per-named-storm windstorm/hail deductible, HO 01 45 T.3 starts the period when the National Hurricane Center names the storm, ends it 72 hours after discontinuation, and treats all wind/hail loss in the period as one occurrence; B.5 permits that basis only with an explicit policy trigger and duration.

HO 01 45 T.7 permits windstorm/hail exclusion when the insured obtains Texas Windstorm Insurance Association coverage and the applicable exclusion endorsement plus signed acknowledgment at binding are in place; T.1 then does not apply and other policy provisions remain in force.

The appetite guide requires a signed exclusion acknowledgment at binding for the residual-market wind/hail exclusion path, and the referral matrix requires internal referral whenever windstorm/hail will be excluded and placed in a residual market.

HO 01 45 T.4 extends the HO-3 2018-09 S.4 action limitation from two years after loss to two years and one day after the loss date; the cross-reference should not be silently transposed to HO-3 2011-05 because its action provision is S.3 and its S.4 is the deductible provision.

HO 01 45 T.5 requires claim acknowledgement within 15 days, written approval or denial within 15 business days after receipt of all reasonably requested items, and payment within 5 business days after an approval notice; HO-3 2018-09 S.3 separately states its proof-of-loss-plus-resolution payment trigger.
HO-3 2018-09 S.1-S.2 requires prompt notice, property protection, damaged-personal-property inventory, and a signed sworn proof of loss within 60 days after the insurer requests it.
B-2021-08 applies to residential property policies delivered or issued for delivery in Texas with an effective date on or after 2022-01-01, and it supersedes B-2016-04.
HO 01 45 edition 2022-01 attaches to HO-3, is effective for policies with an effective date on or after 2022-01-01, and governs where it conflicts with the attached form.

The Texas windstorm deductible overlay treats the bulletin, the HO 01 45 amendment, and internal underwriting guidance as separate layers with different roles; the internal guide is not part of the policy contract and cannot be quoted to an insured or claimant.

A windstorm or hail deductible under B-2021-08 may be a percentage of Coverage A between 1% and 5%, may reach 10% in the seacoast territories defined in B.6, or may be a flat-dollar deductible that is not less than the policy's all-other-perils deductible; the insurer must file the applicable amendatory endorsement and rate rule before applying the deductible.

HO 01 45 T.1 implements the Texas separate windstorm and hail deductible as a Declarations percentage of Coverage A in the 1% to 5% range, with a 10% ceiling in the seacoast territories, and does not itself add a flat-dollar deductible.

B-2021-08 requires the separate windstorm and hail deductible to be disclosed on the Declarations page in type no smaller than the all-other-perils deductible and to show both the percentage and the corresponding dollar amount at the Coverage A limit in effect at issuance.

For any increase in the windstorm and hail deductible percentage, B-2021-08 requires written notice at least 30 days before the renewal effective date; if notice is not provided, the increase does not take effect for that renewal term and the prior percentage continues.

For a windstorm or hail loss, only the separate windstorm and hail deductible applies and the all-other-perils deductible is not also applied; when windstorm or hail loss shares an occurrence with another covered peril, the loss is either allocated by peril or, if allocation is impossible, subject to only the larger single deductible.

If the Declarations select a per-named-storm deductible, the named-storm period begins when the National Hurricane Center names the storm and ends 72 hours after the designation is discontinued, and all windstorm and hail loss during that period is treated as a single occurrence for deductible purposes.

HO 01 45 T.7 allows windstorm and hail to be excluded only when the insured obtains that coverage through the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association and the applicable exclusion endorsement is attached with the insured's signed acknowledgment at binding; when excluded that way, T.1 does not apply and the other policy provisions remain in force.

The Texas appetite guide and referral matrix treat residual-market wind and hail exclusion as an internal control: the guide requires a signed exclusion acknowledgment at binding, the referral matrix requires mandatory referral for any risk where windstorm and hail will be excluded and placed in a residual market, and neither source can override a filing, bulletin, attachment, or acknowledgment condition.

HO 01 45 changes the claims timeline by extending the action limitation in S.4 to two years and one day after the date of loss and adding prompt-payment milestones to acknowledge the claim within 15 days, approve or deny in writing within 15 business days after receiving all reasonably requested items, and pay within 5 business days after approval.

When handling a Texas windstorm or hail claim, the operational record needs the policy effective and written dates, state, selected base-form edition, Declarations Coverage A and deductible values, attached endorsement editions, renewal notice, loss date and peril facts, allocation evidence, and relevant named-storm timestamps.

The Texas overlay's focused checks are to verify applicability and assembly, configuration and renewal, wind/hail loss allocation, named-storm and exclusion conditions, claims timing, and internal referral controls before a deductible decision is made.
